# Critique — Pattern 11 (Fitness History)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Activity Baseline (~10%), Cardiovascular Training & Endurance (~15%), Strength, Mobility, & Combat (~20%), Athletic History & Training Tools (~25%), Recovery, Injury History, & Goals (~20%), and self-monitoring/tracking fillers (~10%). Reaching the 255-question limit was relatively straightforward, though a few self-monitoring questions (positions 245–255) served as minor fillers; had the limit been larger, more specific sport-specific technique and periodization questions would have been drafted. Overlaps exist with the Cardiovascular and Musculoskeletal domains (e.g., regular exercise habits, orthopedic surgery history) because physical capabilities and joint stability directly determine safe fitness options. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions representing positive fitness markers, athletic compliance, and recovery habits (e.g., running regularly, tracking heart rate zones, using saunas, prioritizing sleep) to align with a convention where a stored bit `1` represents sedentary status, injury, or lack of structured training. We paraphrased concepts from the IPAQ and PAR-Q+ to keep the questions accessible and non-copyrighted. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your fitness history symptoms weekly...") as the term "fitness symptoms" is awkward and clinically ambiguous.
